channel.title: Optimum Chiropractic Care Blog
channel.description: Articles on whiplash, spinal trauma and recovery from Dr. Jordan Moore, Optimum Chiropractic Care, Mobile, AL.

item.title: Central Sensitization Explained: Why Pain Can Outlast the Injury
item.description: A plain-language look at central sensitization: how the nervous system can amplify pain after an injury, features that may point toward it, and how care is approached at Optimum Chiropractic Care in Mobile, Alabama.

item.title: Digital Motion X-Ray Explained: Seeing How the Spine Moves in Real Time
item.description: A plain-language explanation of Digital Motion X-Ray: how video fluoroscopy records the spine in motion, what it can show that still images may not, who may be evaluated with it, and what to expect at a visit in Mobile, Alabama.

item.title: Shockwave Therapy for Stubborn Tendon and Heel Pain: What a Session Involves
item.description: A plain-language look at shockwave therapy: how the Duolith SD1 Ultra delivers acoustic waves, which tendon and heel conditions it is commonly used for, and what to expect at a visit in Mobile, Alabama.

item.title: Why You Should See a Chiropractor After a Car Accident — Even If You Feel Fine
item.description: Feeling okay after a car accident doesn't mean you're uninjured. Dr. Jordan Moore explains why delayed symptoms are common, what can be missed without an evaluation, and why waiting may cost you.

item.title: What Happens to Your Spine in a Car Accident
item.description: A biomechanical explanation of spinal injury mechanisms in motor vehicle collisions — cervical acceleration-deceleration, soft tissue loading, and why early evaluation matters.

item.title: What to Look for in a Chiropractor After a Car Accident
item.description: Not all chiropractic practices are equally equipped to evaluate and treat trauma patients. Here's what credentials, tools, and clinical experience actually matter.

item.title: Why Whiplash Symptoms Are Often Delayed
item.description: Many patients feel fine immediately after a car accident — only to develop neck pain, headaches, or cognitive symptoms days later. Here's the clinical explanation.
